An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 12.10 A 3
div.ab: Ille uero dicebatur uiceconsul qui, consule absente, ipsius uices supplebat in iure et in foro.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 639 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 12, 10, and numbers 12, 10 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 12, 10 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
div.ab: And he was called vice-consul who, in the consul's absence, took his place in law and in court.
